import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I wrote a plan for the `/` → `#` alias. It passed validation and `sase plan propose` has staged it for your approval. No code has changed in either repo, and no finalizer declaration was needed.

**Mostly a copy of the `\` alias.** bob's `expand_sigil_alias` handles `/` the same way it handles `\`. It swaps `/` for `#` only where its completion grammar says a real `#` would open a menu, never at a line start. A second `/` right away leaves one literal `/` and closes the menu, at any typing speed. Undo restores the `/`. In Mac Capture, the double-tap arm and the fast-tap re-ask now remember which key bob replaced, so `\` and `/` each undo only their own alias.

**One new rule, because `/` already means things that `\` never did.** I tested today's `bob` build on a throwaway vault. A straight copy of the `\` rule would break these:

| You type | Today | What a straight copy would do |
|---|---|---|
| `=/` | starts a split | turns it into a named start (`=#`) |
| `[[folder/` | completes note paths | jumps to headings |
| `=/fix/`, `=*fix/` | Pomodoro names, which can contain `/` | swaps the `/` for `#` |

So the plan keeps a `/` literal wherever bob already reads it as part of a field. The one exception is block-ID fields: an ID can never contain `/`, so `@cash+goog-exit/` and `@cash:goog-exit/` still open the drawer and Pomodoro-name menus. Routes can't contain `/` either, so `@cash/` still opens sections. `\` keeps working in all the excluded spots, and a blank-draft `/` still opens Go To exactly as today.

**One decision for you at approval: `after_space`** (default `alias`). Should a `/` typed after a space also open the type menu (`Buy milk /`) and the drawer-bullet menu (`- /`), like `\` does? The cost is that a spaced ` / ` or a path like ` /usr/bin` then needs `/` `/` first. Slashes glued to text (`11/5`, `w/`, `and/or`, URLs, `~/x`) are never touched. Pick `literal` if you only want `/` to work glued to a marker, such as `@cash/` or `=25/`.

**Docs:** Mac Capture's `keyboard.md` is already 16 words over its 6,000-word cap, so the docs check fails before any change. The plan adds `/` to the existing `\` row instead of adding a new row, and trims nearby wording until the page is back under the cap.
